institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Inside the EU and therefore it was possible from an economic perspective. I really like France and Paris and therefore i felt safe going there

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Difficult.. I don't think anyone thinks this is easy, but the host university replied quickly to e-mails

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I paid to be part of the elcomme eek whoch gave a good introduction to the university, but was a bit pricy

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Difficult. I was lucky enough to find housing in Cite Universitaire, but not in FOndation Danoise hich I applied for. The quality of the houses differ a lotand I as not so lucky with my house but met a lot of seet people from the other houses, so although my acommodation was not that good I did have a good time.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is way nicer to live off campus and have a lower rent so you can actually go out and use your money on things other than rent

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very stressful, and a lot of the courses were full when they opened the registration for exchange students

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is first come forst served and just very chaotic and stressful

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not uch, I think you could apply to change courses after registration but they have very harsh deadlines

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite lucky and got some of the courses I planned to attend, but others I did not get and I just had to pick something in the stressful minutes when they opened up for registration

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan a lot of back-up courses. Exchange students are allowed to register later than local students and there fore you must have many back up plans

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level would be higher, but I think it is just differences between having professors who also practise other jobs and professors who only do research related and education

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite different, much more engaging and interactive, but also more slow

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Religion and populism, defence economics, global inequality and sustainability, the ICC and human rights, evaluating human capital policies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Global inequality and sustainability and the ICC and human rights were very good. However, the ICC and human rights were quite difficult if you are not a law student (I am a political science student myself)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. I was quite prepared that it would be expensive, and did not want to say no to an experience while I was abroad

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was cheaper than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports clus like simming, cinema clubs and other sorts of things. But I mainly spent my time with other exchange students

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go out and explore the city on your own! You will spend so much time with a lot of other people and ne friends but I definitely recommend going out in the city on your own as well

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Lyon for a weekend and to SOuth of France - definitely recommend using the fast trains doing stuff like that!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. It is difficult to interact with local students but I think it is like that a lot of places, unfortunately.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The calmness of such a big city. Everyone doing things in their tempo. much more reading books and less smartphones

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It is difficult in the beginning but it gets better and will be such af great experience!! Go out and meet people - every other exchange student will be happy to talk to you and prioritize alone time as well, so you don't burn out

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the new friends I met

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Settling in, I found it very difficult

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
